title: TPS — Intermediate
summary: Project JOHNO in third person: a shoulder camera with GASP, relevance, ballistics and heat, limb medical, a ten-slot gunsmith, a vehicle throttle, and a save.

sections.title: Shoulder camera and GASP
sections.why: Aiming pulls the shoulder camera in. Motion matching does not trace.
reading: The intermediate third-person camera shares the pawn with GASP motion matching. IA_Aim traces from the camera and sets Aiming. The shoulder boom reads that bool and shortens. GASP reads Speed and the trajectory. It does not read the trace, and it must not fire a second trace to decide whether the camera is tight. The excerpt is Graph_IA_Aim: a visibility trace, then Aiming = true when bHit is set. Release still has to clear the bool. This graph is the camera preset, not the interact preset.

Project JOHNO's over-the-shoulder pose changes when Aiming is true: the database picks an aim set instead of a hip set. That selection is a query. Putting it on Tick re-queries while the button is held and the result has not changed. The mapping context can put IA_Aim on a shoulder button without the graph knowing the device.

Movement writes Speed. If the aim pose also writes Speed, the gait and the camera fight and the mesh twists. A heavy aim may scale Speed in one function after the movement write. It does not replace IA_Move. The weapon reads Aiming for spread. The vehicle, when the player is driving, disables this boom instead of running IA_Aim into the seat.
Save can store Aiming. The boom transform is derived. AOI does not care about the camera. Relevance is about the pawn.

The figure is the real Camera aim graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Aim is the shoulder button. The boom camera reads Aiming. The aim trace starts at the camera, not at the feet. A hit means we are aiming at a target. True pulls the camera in. The camera component reads this. Do not move the boom on Tick. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 10 is `FHitResult Hit_tpl_camera_trace; bool bHit_tpl_camera_trace = false; if (UWorld* World_tpl_camera_trace = GetW`. Line 13 is `Aiming = true; // node:tpl_camera_set`.

Across this track, keep IA_Aim, Aiming, GASP distinct. Aiming pulls the shoulder camera in. Motion matching does not trace. GASP reads Aiming. Graph_IA_Aim sets Aiming = true. It does not write Speed.

sections.title: Motion-matched movement
sections.why: Speed is 600 or 200 from IA_Move. The shoulder camera does not write it.
reading: Third-person motion matching needs a gait before it needs a camera. IA_Move greater than zero writes Speed = 600.f. Otherwise the excerpt writes Speed = 200.f. GASP builds a trajectory from that speed. The shoulder camera's Aiming bool can select an aim set. It is not a second speed. If both graphs assign Speed, the last write in the frame wins and the trajectory pops.

The function is Graph_IA_Move. There is no Tick. A Tick write would also run while the player is in the gunsmith radial, and the on-foot database would keep sprinting under a menu. Crouch and prone are extra literals in the same branch, chosen by a stance the ability sets, not by the camera distance.

The vehicle throttle is a different variable on a different component. Copying Speed into Throttle makes the car use the on-foot numbers. AOI replicates the pawn, not the trajectory. Clients run the same database from the replicated speed. The pose itself stays local.

Save stores Speed only if the mode resumes a sprint. It does not store the chosen animation. The reload graph does not write Speed either, even if a heavy mag should slow the pawn. That slow is one multiply after this write.

The figure is the real Movement graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Move is the axis. The character movement component consumes Speed. Zero axis means the stick is released. Greater than zero means the player is pushing move. A live axis takes the fast path. A released axis walks. Sprint speed. Walk speed. Write sprint speed. Write walk speed. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 9 is `Speed = 600.f; // node:tpl_movement_sprint`. Line 13 is `Speed = 200.f; // node:tpl_movement_walk`.

Across this track, keep IA_Move, Speed, GASP distinct. Speed is 600 or 200 from IA_Move. The shoulder camera does not write it. IA_Move > 0.f chooses Speed = 600.f or Speed = 200.f. Aiming does not assign Speed.

assignment.model: IA_Move > 0.f chooses Speed = 600.f or Speed = 200.f. Aiming does not assign Speed.

sections.title: Third-person relevance
sections.why: Distant third-person pawns drop out on the 0.5s CheckAOI timer.
reading: A third-person pawn is expensive to replicate because the mesh is large and the animation is busy. Area of interest drops pawns the player cannot see. The sample starts CheckAOI from Begin Play on a 0.5 second looping timer. The authority traces. The excerpt assigns Relevant = bHit. Clients that are not relevant do not receive the pawn, so they also do not receive its GASP speed or its equipped id.

The HasAuthority test in the excerpt is an empty block before the trace. Nest the relevance write inside it. A client that sets Relevant on its own pawn pulls every cosmetic the server had culled, including other players' shoulder cameras. The camera is not replicated. The pawn is.

The weapon, the limbs, and the gunsmith id replicate only while Relevant is true. They do not run their own timers. A vehicle the player can hear but not see may stay relevant by a larger radius. That radius is data on the vehicle, not a tick of every wheel. Debris from destruction should leave relevance quickly.

Shortening 0.5 to every frame turns the pass into Tick. Lengthening it makes pop-in obvious on a third-person mesh, which is large on screen. 0.5 is the sample. The replication graph is the production system that replaces the trace.

The figure is the real Area of interest graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. Begin Play starts the relevance timer. Relevance is checked twice a second, not every frame. CheckAOI is the relevancy pass. The server decides who is relevant. A stand-in for distance. A real AOI uses the replication graph. Relevant gates replication. The widget is not replicated. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 10 is `if (UWorld* World = GetWorld()) { FTimerHandle Timer_tpl_aoi_timer; World->GetTimerManager().SetTimer(Timer_tp`. Line 15 is `if (HasAuthority()) { /* authority */ } // node:tpl_aoi_auth`.

Across this track, keep CheckAOI, Relevant, Has Authority distinct. Distant third-person pawns drop out on the 0.5s CheckAOI timer. CheckAOI runs every 0.5f. Relevant = bHit belongs inside HasAuthority.

sections.title: Third-person shots, wear, and heat
sections.why: IA_Fire traces once. Heat steps by 0.05. The shoulder camera does not fire.
reading: Third-person fire starts at IA_Fire, not at the shoulder camera and not at Tick. The excerpt traces and, on a hit, does Heat = (Heat + 0.05f). Wear is the sibling float on the same weapon. The visible muzzle on the third-person mesh is a local effect from the action. It is not a replicated projectile. A miss in the sample adds no heat. A real barrel still heats. Damage waits for the hit. Heat should not.

Aiming tightens spread by reading the camera bool before the trace direction is built. The camera graph does not add heat. If it did, aiming down the sights would cook the barrel. The magazine graph still owns Magazine and Reserve. This function must not decrement them.

Replicating each pellet's transform, so other players see the third-person tracer, is the expensive version. A tracer is a cosmetic spawned from the fire event on proxies that already have the pawn because it is relevant. Heat and wear replicate as floats, from the authority. The gunsmith asset names the heat step for the equipped barrel.
A vehicle cannon does not reuse this Heat. Limbs receive damage through Any Damage. Save stores heat and wear with EquippedId. AOI already decided whether the shooter exists for a given client.

The figure is the real Ballistics graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Fire is the shot. Wear and heat update here. The trace is the sample projectile. A physical projectile would replace this node, not Tick. A hit applies damage. A miss still adds heat. Heat plus a step. Current heat. One shot of heat. Write heat on the weapon component. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 10 is `FHitResult Hit_tpl_ballistics_trace; bool bHit_tpl_ballistics_trace = false; if (UWorld* World_tpl_ballistics_`. Line 13 is `Heat = (Heat + 0.05f); // node:tpl_ballistics_set`.

Across this track, keep IA_Fire, Heat, Wear distinct. IA_Fire traces once. Heat steps by 0.05. The shoulder camera does not fire. IA_Fire adds Heat = (Heat + 0.05f). Aiming only tightens spread. Tracers are local cosmetics on relevant proxies.

assignment.prompt: Third-person tracers replicate per pellet and heat rises while aiming. Which action should add heat, and what is the excerpt's assignment?
assignment.model: IA_Fire adds Heat = (Heat + 0.05f). Aiming only tightens spread. Tracers are local cosmetics on relevant proxies.

sections.title: Third-person limb medical
sections.why: The server writes the limb. A normal hit stops at 10% of max. OnRep plays the limp.
reading: Other players see a third-person limp, so the limb float has to be one number. Any Damage is the event. The excerpt assigns Health = 90.f after an empty HasAuthority block. Nest the write, and replace 90 with the clamped result. Project JOHNO's rule: a normal hit does not drop a limb below 10% of its max. A max of 50 floors at 5. Crossing zero is a downed state, not this clamp.

OnRep_Health is where the third-person mesh limps. Everyone who has the pawn relevant plays that reaction from the float. Subtracting inside OnRep makes the limp worse on every machine that receives the property. The local camera shake is also the notify, and only on the owning client.

Ballistics calls the event. The gunsmith does not. A medic item in the inventory calls the same event with healing, still on the authority, and the clamp also caps the heal at max. Save stores the limb after the server write. The shoulder camera does not store a copy of the limb.
A client that writes the limb so the third-person body reacts early will snap when the server float arrives. Play the reaction from the notify. Do not invent the number.

The figure is the real Replicated health graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. Any Damage is the request. Authority decides. Has Authority keeps the change on the server. A stand-in for health after the hit. Set the replicated health. OnRep runs on the clients that hear the property. The UI listens. It does not decide the number. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 9 is `if (HasAuthority()) { /* authority */ } // node:tpl_replicated-health_auth`. Line 10 is `Health = 90.f; // node:tpl_replicated-health_set`.

Across this track, keep Any Damage, Has Authority, 10% clamp distinct. The server writes the limb. A normal hit stops at 10% of max. OnRep plays the limp. Inside HasAuthority, clamp to 10% of max, which is 5 when max is 50. OnRep plays the limp.

assignment.model: Inside HasAuthority, clamp to 10% of max, which is 5 when max is 50. OnRep plays the limp.

sections.title: Ten-slot gunsmith on the body
sections.why: The third-person mesh builds from EquippedId. Ten slots stay in the asset.
reading: The third-person body shows the weapon other players see, so the equipped id has to match. The gunsmith record has ten slots. IA_Equip, from a number key or from the radial menu, is the selection. The excerpt assigns EquippedId = IA_Equip after an empty HasAuthority block. Nest that write. The owning client and the proxies build the mesh from the asset. They do not each invent an id.

Replicating ten socket transforms so the third-person magazine, optic, and barrel match is the expensive version. One id is enough, and the asset says which socket each slot uses. Wear and heat hang off the equipped weapon. A cosmetic slot does not reset heat unless it is the barrel.

GASP may change the aim pose when the id changes, by reading the asset's anim set. It does not write EquippedId. The camera does not. Inventory holds the item that points at the same asset. Save stores the id. AOI means a non-relevant pawn does not send the id at all.
A client that writes the id locally shows a weapon the server will replace, and the third-person mesh pops in other players' views. That pop is the bug the authority gate prevents.

The figure is the real Gunsmith graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Equip picks a slot. The radial menu can send the same action. The server decides the equipped id. Replicate EquippedId. The client builds the mesh from the data asset. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 7 is `if (HasAuthority()) { /* authority */ } // node:tpl_gunsmith_auth`. Line 8 is `EquippedId = IA_Equip; // node:tpl_gunsmith_set`.

Across this track, keep IA_Equip, EquippedId, Ten slots distinct. The third-person mesh builds from EquippedId. Ten slots stay in the asset. EquippedId = IA_Equip inside HasAuthority. Ten slots stay in the asset. Proxies build the mesh.

sections.title: Vehicle throttle
sections.why: IA_Throttle is the axis. The server writes Throttle. The on-foot Speed stays separate.
reading: Leaving the third-person pawn for a vehicle is a different component. IA_Throttle is the axis. The excerpt tests HasAuthority in an empty block and assigns Throttle = IA_Throttle. Nest the write. The chaos vehicle reads Throttle. It does not read the on-foot Speed of 600 or 200. Copying Speed into Throttle launches the car at a sprint number that means something else.

The shoulder camera disables while seated. IA_Aim does not steer. The gunsmith id may name a mounted weapon, and that weapon's heat is not the rifle's Heat. Artillery, if the vehicle is a gun, spends shells on its own event. It does not add 0.05 to the rifle. Wheels are local meshes driven by the simulated throttle. Replicating each wheel transform is the expensive version.

AOI for a vehicle can use a larger radius, because a truck is visible farther than a person. That is data, not a tick of the suspension. The player pawn's GASP database pauses while seated. It does not keep writing Speed into the vehicle.

Save stores Throttle only if the mode restores a moving vehicle. More often it stores fuel, which is a sibling of the economy's supplies, and the vehicle id. The on-foot slot and the vehicle slot can share a struct layout. They should not share the Speed field.

The figure is the real Vehicle drive graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Throttle is the axis. The chaos vehicle reads Throttle. The server owns the velocity. Write the axis. Do not replicate the wheel meshes. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 7 is `if (HasAuthority()) { /* authority */ } // node:tpl_vehicle-drive_auth`. Line 8 is `Throttle = IA_Throttle; // node:tpl_vehicle-drive_set`.

Across this track, keep IA_Throttle, Has Authority, Throttle distinct. IA_Throttle is the axis. The server writes Throttle. The on-foot Speed stays separate. Throttle = IA_Throttle inside HasAuthority. Speed stays on the pawn. The shoulder camera disables.

sections.title: Save the third-person kit
sections.why: Begin Play loads limbs, heat, the equipped id, and fuel. Not the pose.
reading: The intermediate third-person slot packs the limb floats, Heat, wear, Magazine, Reserve, EquippedId, and vehicle fuel if the mode has a car. It does not pack the GASP pose, the boom transform, or Relevant. Begin Play loads, because the mesh, the camera, and the vehicle component exist. The excerpt assigns SlotValue = 1.f from a vector stand-in and LoadSlot logs Loaded.

Tick would store a half-applied limp and a throttle from the middle of a gear change. Autosave is an event on a slow timer, using the same struct. The authority writes the limbs and EquippedId before the pack. AOI relevance is recomputed after load from positions, not restored as a bool that has gone stale.

The on-foot Speed is optional. The pose is not. Clients rebuild the pose from Speed and Aiming once those exist. The ten gunsmith slots are not ten meshes in the file. The id selects the asset that is already in the project.
Load order matters. Apply EquippedId before the mesh builds, apply Aiming before the boom extends, and start the vehicle simulation after fuel is set. The constructor is too early for all three.

The figure is the real Save / load slot graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. Begin Play writes the slot once. Do not write it from Tick. The member written into the payload. Make Struct builds the save payload. Keep the member on the component. Load is its own event. It does not run during the save. Break Struct reads one member. A print stands in for the load UI. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 8 is `FVector Made_tpl_saveload_make = FVector::ZeroVector; Made_tpl_saveload_make.X = 1.f; Made_tpl_saveload_make.Y`. Line 9 is `SlotValue = 1.f; // node:tpl_save-load_store`.

Across this track, keep Begin Play, SlotValue, LoadSlot distinct. Begin Play loads limbs, heat, the equipped id, and fuel. Not the pose. Begin Play loads. EquippedId is stored. The pose and the boom are derived.
